## A saved comparison you can hold against our published numbers

`raw_forecast_reference` now carries two values per slot instead of one.

`value` is what it was in 1.12.0: the first forecast this installation ever
received for that slot. How far ahead that was depends on your horizon - two
days, or five.

`final_value` is new: the last forecast before the official price arrived.
That is the moment the market replaced the guess, and it is the same point in
time the published forecast-quality figures measure. A chart drawn on it can
therefore be compared with the hit rates on the quality page, which a line
frozen five days earlier could not.

- While a slot is still a forecast, `final_value` follows every update. The
  first official price settles it, and a forecast the API falls back to
  afterwards cannot overwrite what was predicted before the market spoke.
- `final_captured_at` says when that last forecast was received, in local
  observation time rather than model run time.
- The ApexCharts example now draws `final_value` and falls back to `value`
  for slots that were saved before this update, so an existing card keeps
  working either way.
- A slot first seen with an official price still yields no reference at all.
  Nothing is reconstructed after the fact.

## Charging windows in quarter hours

The best-window duration moves in steps of 0.25 hours. A charge that takes
three and a half hours can now ask for 3.5 instead of asking for 3 and coming
up short, or for 4 and paying for an hour it does not use. The API has priced
such windows all along; only the setup dialog insisted on whole hours.

One caveat, stated here rather than discovered later: the measured forecast
quality is published per whole hour, so a 3.5-hour window is reported with
the figures of the 3-hour one.

## Updating from 1.12.x

Nothing to configure. Snapshots already saved keep their `value`; `final_value`
appears for every slot from the next update on. Copy the card from the README
again if you want the comparable line. Existing entries keep the whole-hour
window they were set up with; the quarter hours are there when you want them.
